title: Robertstad v. North Texas Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint found administratively out of order and unable to be put in order for failure to comply with BCO 43-3: initial e-mail filing was not permitted, and hard-copy filing was after the 30-day deadline. No merits determination. The SJC approved by roll call, 21 concur, 3 absent.
first_summary: Robertstad's complaint against North Texas Presbytery was dismissed by the SJC because he filed by e-mail rather than hard copy. The SJC did not reach the merits; a concurrence explained BCO 43-3 and suggested an amendment.
summary: The SJC found TE Arnold Robertstad's complaint against North Texas Presbytery administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order under BCO 43-3. Robertstad initially filed by e-mail—not an allowed filing—and his hard-copy filing arrived after the thirty-day deadline. The SJC reasoned that BCO 42-4/43-3 notification language concerns a lower court notifying parties, not party e-filing, and OMSJC 18.10.b bars e-mail filing. The merits were not reached; a concurrence urged later clarification by amendment, and no further proceedings are indicated.
